topics.title: Mansa Musa: The Gold Behind a King's Journey
topics.text: Mansa Musa spent so much gold in Cairo that its price reportedly dropped and failed to recover for more than a decade.
topics.meaning: Reportedly preserves al-Umari's attribution of a decline in gold's exchange value to the party's spending. His account describes about twelve years, not multiple decades, halving, or an independently established economy-wide crash. Develop the spending and prolonged effect before court protocol.

topics.title: The Letter That Split the Atom
topics.text: The discovery that opened the nuclear age started with an accident.
topics.meaning: Accident means an unexpected discovery during deliberate research, not a spill, equipment failure, or other laboratory mishap. Follow with the actual story, without a disclaimer correcting this ordinary use of the word.

topics.title: The Coldest Place on Earth Was a House in Leiden
topics.text: There is a limit to how cold anything can get—and near that limit, scientists found electricity could flow without resistance.
topics.meaning: Researchers approached absolute zero; they did not reach it. Resistance-free current refers to superconductivity under suitable conditions, not every material.

topics.title: Ten Sheets of Glass in a Berkeley Basement
topics.text: Einstein helped create quantum physics, but its success left him questioning whether it described reality or only what scientists could observe.
topics.meaning: The successful theory and Einstein's completeness objection establish the premise. The story must narrow this to what Bell tests actually constrain; it must not claim every question about reality was settled.
alternatives: Quantum physics worked—but did nature really need its strange rules, or was a more familiar explanation waiting underneath?

topics.title: The Carpenter Who Solved the Ocean
topics.text: A compass tells you which way you’re going, but not where you are. For centuries, that gap could cost sailors their lives—and a carpenter helped close it with a clock.
topics.meaning: The familiar distinction between compass direction and position establishes the missing capability. The risk to sailors makes the clock consequential. Harrison helped improve longitude measurement; the claim does not say a clock alone supplies a complete fix, that every ship gained one immediately, or that shipwrecks ended.
